summary:
Andalucía stands under Spain's national framework: Ley 4/2023 of 28 February 2023, published in the Boletín Oficial del Estado, applies uniformly across all autonomous communities and governs the regional position. The law covers the real and effective equality of trans persons and the guarantee of LGBTI rights.

Any person aged 16 or over may rectify the gender mention on their own civil registry entry directly before the Civil Registry. The right to the registered change is grounded in the free development of personality under Article 10.1 of the Constitution, and adults may rectify the registered sex entry without prior surgical reassignment. This administrative route replaced the former requirement of a gender-dysphoria diagnosis and two years of medical treatment. Recognition is possible from age 12 under conditions, a provision that proved contentious during the parliamentary passage of the law.

Access to sex-separated facilities rests on the gender marker recorded in the civil registry rather than on biological sex, so the entry obtained through self-declaration is the operative basis for facility rules in Spain. This contrasts with the stricter single-sex-space approach being adopted in the United Kingdom on biological-sex lines, applied case by case rather than as a blanket ban.

The national framework defines and sanctions discriminatory conduct and harassment on grounds of sexual orientation, sexual identity, gender expression and sexual characteristics. It also declares discriminatory contract clauses null and void, obliges collection of discrimination data broken down by the causes covered, and mandates measures adapted to rural circumstances. Human Rights Watch recorded on 16 February 2023 that the law strengthens protections for unmarried same-sex couples and combats LGBTI discrimination in healthcare, employment and housing.
tangentialFactors:
There is no free-standing criminal offence of gender-expression-based hate crime in Spain: the phrase appears in no article of the Spanish Criminal Code. The hate-speech aggravating circumstance in Article 22.4 and the penalties of Article 510, one to four years' imprisonment plus a fine of six to twelve months, derive from Organic Law 6/2022.

Enforcement of the gender-identity aggravation is documented at first-instance level outside Andalucía. In July 2026 a Tribunal de Instancia in Vigo applied the transfobia aggravating circumstance for the first time in a misdemeanour case over WhatsApp threats sent to a trans woman, fining the author EUR 300. In a case reported on 8 January 2026 in Valencia, a juvenile gang harassed, insulted, beat and filmed a trans person in a park to mock them; the sole adult defendant received six months' prison and two minors were judged separately.

Spain's administrative self-declaration regime places it alongside Argentina, Ireland, Portugal and Uruguay. A 2016 survey of 23 countries ranked Spain the most trans-supportive of the group surveyed and the only country where a majority supported unrestricted legal gender designation change; that ranking predates the 2023 law.
localsOnly:
For residents of Andalucía, the rectification procedure runs as an ordinary administrative act before the Civil Registry, with no requirement of a diagnosis, judicial authorisation or medical treatment. The same registry entry governs subsequent dealings with regional Andalucian services that key off the recorded gender marker.

Ley 4/2023 also applies to residents through anti-discrimination duties with a regional operational edge: employers, service providers and public bodies in Andalucía must collect discrimination data broken down by the covered causes, and the statute mandates measures adapted to rural circumstances, relevant to the province's interior. Contracts containing discriminatory clauses are null and void for residents who encounter them in employment, housing or insurance.

Other operative provisions in force for Andalucian residents include the ban on non-consensual normalising surgeries on intersex children, expanded assisted reproduction rules, parental recognition for unmarried same-sex couples, strengthened sexuality education, and anti-discrimination coverage in healthcare, employment and housing. Same-sex marriage and full adoption rights have been in force since 2005, and legal gender change does not require surgery or sterilisation.
outOfScopeNotes:
The source inventory for this record contains national provisions only. No Andalucía-specific Civil Registry office procedure, regional implementing decree, or regional enforcement decision is documented here, so the practical steps a visitor would take in Málaga, Sevilla or Granada beyond the national administrative route remain unresolved and not sourced.

The comparative ranking cited is a 2016 baseline and predates Ley 4/2023; no post-2023 survey of Spanish public opinion is available in this inventory. Likewise, no documented case of a trans visitor being refused facility access on Andalucian territory is sourced, and the enforcement examples recorded here come from Vigo and Valencia, in other autonomous communities.
